candidates.text: After that trailer they dropped they expect us to cheer for the avengers to win gang? 😂 Doom in 4

Some meta level observations:

1) Dario’s tweets benefit from scarcity. The fact that he doesn’t “spend much time” on X makes a tweet carry more weight and is itself a statement of seriousness

2) He (and Sholto) selected the right person to engage with. Gavin is an ideal steelman; he’s a legit critic but is civil and well informed. Having him as the interlocutor makes everyone look better and makes for a stronger debate

3) Going direct with a personal post was the escalation after a senior colleague (ie Sholto) already did the fact checking and elevated the debate to the level of principles. So Dario was able to come in and focus on his beliefs rather than having to first debate the details of who said what when

4) The personal post was actually personal. Parts like the story about his father make it less likely to read like PR ghostwriting, and thus give it more power. The personal story also makes the post more memorable because it’s specific and concrete and relatable 

5) The argument in part 2 is an interesting insight into how he assesses his own messaging. When accused of negative messaging (qualitative), he rebuts that it’s roughly balanced in large part because he’s written one essay about benefits and one about risks (quantitative). Implication: he’s taking an analytical approach to measuring positivity, but many others are simply going off vibes - so this won’t be the last time he and his critics talk past each other

candidates.text:
Why did Josh Kushner buy the Lakers?

It has nothing to do with ‘sports as an asset class’ as The Economist suggests. 

It’s a powerful tax shield. 

My guess is he is preparing to offset a boatload of carried interest income. 

If you own a sports team, done correctly, you can get a deduction against income. 

The goal in acquiring a sports team is to setup a ‘non-passive’ deduction. 

(A passive deduction can only offset passive income.)

Active deduction follows because of ‘material participation’ under Rule 469.

It gets better. 

The amount you can deduct year is based on a 15 year depreciation schedule.

That’s faster than the 27.5 year deduction found in residential real estate investments. 

So, why now?

Kushner is about to see his W2 carried interest explore from his SpacEx, Stripe, and OpenAI investments. 

That’s it. 

Is it a free lunch?

No. There is ‘depreciation recapture’ at sale. Still, you are compounding on the deferred tax bill. 

I wouldn’t be surprised if he is waiving his salary - typical for sports team owners. 

What happens when you combine Investing, Tax, and Estate coherently?

That’s called Wealth Architecture.

candidates.text:
I am so happy to see that revamping Indian government schools is finally being taken this seriously.

This is very personal for me.

Both my parents started their careers as teachers in government schools. Two young married kids, both raised in poverty, first in their bloodline to be educated, ambitious to give their kids a world class education.

They worked really hard and moved up the ladder quite quickly. My father retired last month as an Administrative Officer in the state health department. He had initially headed the education department, but was disqualified for a Class I officer position because he spoke too honestly in his MPSC interview.

My mother is still very committed to teaching and was recently transferred to a government school around 50km from my house. The roads are horrendous and during the rainy season, it is genuinely very hard to reach the school.

Her school does not have a girls' washroom.

My mom has got kidney stones more times than I can remember at this point.

Both my parents used to travel to nearby villages on bikes and scooters and have gotten into some very serious accidents because of the roads. I have some of those memories etched in my brain.

And then there are the kids.

Every year, we sponsor books, clothes and other things for some of the kids. We also arrange their travel to and fro, pick them up and drop them back home, just so that coming to school is one less thing their families have to worry about.

And I keep thinking, isn't this literally what the government should be doing? But nvm.

A lot of parents don't want to send their kids to government schools anymore because of the quality of education and because they don't see any future promise in it. They would rather have their kids start working early and contribute to the family.

My parents even tried to build a washroom for the school themselves. They were refused permission.

So when I see the protests happening around the country and the attention towards government schools, it genuinely makes me happy.

Because I have seen how hollow the system can be.

And I really do think education should be one of the biggest priorities in our development. Everything else comes after giving a child a fair shot at a good education.
